question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Reference class of ~9-10 trading-day NDX-minus-SPX price-return windows centers near +0.2pp (QQQ 1yr 26.41% vs SPY 20.98%; 2026 YTD NDX +17.1% vs SPX +13.1% = +0.24pp/biweek). Window is Sep 8-18 (Labor Day Sep 7 closed), 9 sessions, containing CPI Sep 11, a live FOMC Sep 15-16 with a ~52-66% priced 25bp HIKE, Apple's event, Oracle/Adobe earnings and Sep 18 quad witching. Two-directional: NDX beta >1 plus rate-hike/duration risk into weak September seasonality argues for underperformance (Sep 4 post-payrolls NQ -1.11% vs ES -0.59%), while re-accelerating AI momentum (Nvidia, Dell, Snowflake +16.6%, NDX +4.2% vs SPX +2.7% in August) argues the other way. These roughly cancel, so I sit essentially on the base rate with wide, slightly left-skewed dispersion: 2026 has produced two NDX corrections in which tech fell hard while equal-weight/cyclical benchmarks held up, so the downside tail is fatter than the upside. No prediction market prices this spread at Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold, so there is no crowd anchor; evidence is thin on the specific relative question and I stay near the class prior. Escape mass beyond +/-5pp priced at 3% total: below via an AI-capex/chip panic plus a hawkish hike (the late-July 2026 mechanism), above via a blowout AI catalyst plus a dovish hold.

calls.reference_class: All ~9-10 trading-day (biweekly) windows of Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 price return, 2015-2026, with 2026 weighted for regime

calls.reasoning: Reference class first: over biweekly (9-10 session) windows since 2010 the NDX-SPX price-return spread is roughly symmetric around a small positive median (~+0.15pp), consistent with NDX beating SPX in 12 of the last 16 calendar years. 2026 YTD runs a similar pace (+4.0pp over ~8.2 months, ~+0.2pp per biweek). Adjusting off that anchor: (a) September seasonality is a mild negative for the spread - NDX averages -2.1% in September (2017-2025) vs SPX ~-1.5%, and NDX's ~1.15 beta drags the spread whenever expected index return is negative, with the back half of September historically the weak half; (b) the regime cuts against duration - a Fed HIKE was ~50-52% priced for the Sep 16 FOMC before today's payrolls beat (162k vs 55k expected), and the SEP/dot plot lands inside the window; (c) offsetting positives are the Apple event Sep 9 and Adobe earnings Sep 10, both NDX-overweight, and NDX's +4.2% August. These roughly cancel, so I center essentially at zero (+0.05pp) rather than at the drift. Dispersion is the harder call: VIX at 14.32 is the 2026 low, but the FOMC hike/hold coin flip is a genuinely bimodal driver for tech-vs-broad-market and quad-witching adds flow noise, so I hold the spread near its full reference-class width rather than discounting for the calm tape. Evidence is thin and indirect - no market prices this spread and no source forecasts it - so I stay close to the base rate. Tails past +/-5pp need a ~4-sigma dislocation (AI-financing credit event or hawkish shock on the low side, AI melt-up or flight-to-mega-cap-quality on the high side); priced ~1%/0.7%.

calls.reasoning: Nine sessions (Sep 7 is Labor Day), so this is a dispersion question with signal-to-noise ~0.06 on direction. Class prior is +0.19pp per window and 2026 realized matches it almost exactly (+3.45pp YTD, +5.4pp trailing 1yr). I shrink it ~50%: Big Tech has trailed the S&P for 92% of 2026 and the Mag 7 lagged in H1, so the NDX lead is not durable mega-cap momentum; second-half-September seasonality and a live Sep 16 FOMC where a HIKE is priced 26-66% both cut against high-beta duration, as the Sep 4 payroll tape showed (NQ -1.11% vs ES -0.59%). Offsetting: Apple's Sep 9 event, Adobe Sep 10, NDX sitting ~4% below its 52w high vs SPX ~1.3%, and a possible unadjusted Sep->Dec roll adding ~+0.1pp of carry. Net median +0.10. Width set by the 2026 regime rather than the calm tape, since CPI Sep 11, FOMC with dot plot Sep 16 and quad-witching Sep 18 all sit inside the window. calls.reconciliation: Two real disputes. (1) Dispersion, 2.8 vs 4.1pp: settleable and settled. Run 2 scaled a 2024 monthly spread SD of 1.7pp; Runs 1 and 3 scaled 2026's ~2.5pp. The window is in 2026, a year with two NDX corrections and a SOX bear market, and Run 2's own text says it wants the 'full reference-class width' while pricing something narrower. Adopted the 2026-regime computation (Run 3's basis, which I agree with), shaded down for VIX at its 2026 low, giving 3.95. (2) Median, +0.18 vs +0.05 vs +0.10: pure judgment, no evidence breaks it. I take the shrink-by-half reading because the Mag7-lags-SPX-in-2026 fact (Runs 2 and 3, mutually consistent with NDX leading only via non-Mag7 names) undercuts treating the +0.19pp drift as a persistent factor, while the Sep 4 payroll asymmetry confirms NDX's rate beta into a live FOMC. Unsettleable factuals, left carrying their uncertainty: the futures roll convention (all three flag it; unadjusted would add ~+0.10-0.15pp, part of why I stay positive rather than at zero), the FOMC hike probability quoted at 26/42/52/60-66% across venues (all runs agree the meeting is two-sided, so it widens rather than shifts), and a Sep 2/Sep 3 date collision on which index led, which is pre-window and immaterial. I depart from all three runs on escape mass, pricing 2.5%/1.8% vs their 0.7-1.8%: July 2026 delivered roughly an 8pp monthly spread, ~5pp when scaled to nine sessions, so a repeat of that dispersion regime is a named mechanism rather than a tail abstraction. Market check confirmed across all three runs and the harness: nothing on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers prices relative NDX-vs-SPX performance; only single-index level and FOMC contracts exist, none matching this resolution instrument.

disagreements.verdict: Settled for the wider reading: Run 2 scaled a 2024 monthly SD of 1.7pp, but the window sits in the 2026 regime whose monthly spread SD is ~2.5pp per Run 1's figures and Run 3's July/August evidence. Set 3.95.
